verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “it's been a few days now. I have like a sore and a red skin. It's kind of… It's really itchy,” indicating itchy, red skin for several days.

Patient describes “it's itching a lot” and “my skin is a bit cracked in some parts,” and doctor summarizes “you've got some dry skin and some cracked skin as well, and it's been very itchy,” supporting severe itching with dry, cracked skin.
Patient states, “Mostly like my chest, my… my hands, my arms,” and later clarifies, “just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows,” supporting involvement of chest, hands, and inner elbows.
Patient reports, “I can't even sleep at night… even at work… it's really annoying because I can't actually think about what I have to say,” indicating itching disrupts sleep and work.

Patient says, “I bought like a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night, but it apparently didn't help because it's still itching a lot today,” which matches trying an OTC steroid yesterday with little relief.
Patient notes, “earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema,” and later, “I had eczema before,” confirming a past history of eczema.
Patient responds, “No, I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore?” to medical problems, and later confirms no regular medications, supporting past asthma not currently active or treated.
When asked about other medical problems, patient answers only asthma in the past and “No” to other issues, supporting that no other chronic illnesses are reported.
Doctor asks, “do you take any regular medications at the moment?” Patient: “No,” indicating no current medications.
Doctor: “Do you have any allergies at all?” Patient: “Oh, allergies. No,” confirming no allergies.
Patient states, “So I live with a few flatmates… I'm living with a few people to save money,” confirming living with flatmates.
Patient says, “I work at a pharmaceutical company… I'm a… like a kind of project manager,” confirming employment at a pharmaceutical company.
Doctor: “do you smoke at all?” Patient: “No,” indicating the patient is a non-smoker.
Regarding alcohol, patient says, “I'd say a few… a few beers per week. Something like this,” which supports drinking a few beers per week.
Doctor asks about fevers: “have you noticed any temperature or fevers?” Patient: “No. Just the itching,” confirming no fever.
Doctor asks, “Your chest is okay. No cough?” Patient: “No,” supporting no cough.
Doctor asks, “No. Breathing difficulties?” Patient: “No,” which covers no shortness of breath.
Doctor: “You're passing urine Okay?” Patient: “I think so,” indicating no urinary symptoms are reported.
Doctor asks, “anything on your face at all?” Patient: “Oh, on my face. No,” confirming no facial involvement.
Doctor: “Have you noticed any bleeding… or discharge from your skins?” Patient: “No… You haven't seen any other pus or blood coming out of your skin? No,” confirming no bleeding or discharge.
Doctor summarizes, “you've got some dry skin and some cracked skin as well, and it's been very itchy,” describing the skin as very itchy, dry, and cracked.
Patient specifies, “just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows,” and doctor reiterates chest involvement, supporting that distribution.
Patient denies facial rash: “Oh, on my face. No,” so no facial skin involvement is noted.
Doctor confirms with patient, “You haven't seen any other pus or blood coming out of your skin?… No,” meaning no bleeding or discharge is found/reported.

Patient denies fever, cough, breathing difficulties, and urinary problems (“No… Just the itching… No. Breathing difficulties? No… You're passing urine Okay? I think so”), indicating no systemic symptoms are reported.

Doctor states, “I do wonder whether this is a flare up of your eczema… you mentioned you've got some dry skin and some cracked skin as well, and it's been very itchy… mainly affecting your chest and your back,” while earlier the patient specified chest, hands, and inside elbows; this supports assessment of an acute eczema flare with pruritus and dry, cracked skin in those areas.
Patient: “I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore?” and “do you take any regular medications…? No,” supporting past asthma that is not currently active and needs no regular medications.

Doctor: “I wonder whether giving you stronger prescription of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today… to use… over the next week to 10 days,” matching a stronger topical corticosteroid for about 7–10 days.

Doctor says, “I'm going to give you something, some emollients which helps to moisturize the skin to use in the bath and shower… using the steroids and the emollients on a regular basis over the next week to 10 days,” supporting regular moisturizer use in bath/shower; applying after drying is a reasonable implicit extension but not contradicted.

Doctor: “It's also worth using antihistamines… So things like Loratadine or periton… I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Something like fexofenadine, which I can give to you today,” supporting prescribing fexofenadine and discussing OTC options like loratadine.

Doctor advises, “It's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms. Anything you wear or anything you use in terms of shower gels or soap,” matching advice to keep a trigger diary including products, shower gels, and soaps.

Doctor instructs, “it's definitely worth using that for the first seven to 10 days before we make a decision… But do come back and see me next week if things don't get better,” which implies review in about a week (7–10 days) if not improved.
